original_value: In this paper, we propose a novel strategy to estimate the micro-motion (m-m) of ships from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. To this end, observe that the problem of motion and m-m detection of targets is usually solved using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) along-track interferometry through two radars spatially separated by a baseline along the azimuth direction. The approach proposed in this paper for m-m estimation of ships, occupying thousands of pixels, processes the information generated during the coregistration of several re-synthesized time-domain and not overlapped Doppler sub-apertures. Specifically, the SAR products are generated by splitting the raw data according to a temporally small baseline using one single wide-band staring spotlight (ST) SAR image. The predominant vibrational modes of different ships are then estimated. The performance analysis is conducted on one ST SAR image recorded by COSMO-SkyMed satellite system. Finally, the newly proposed approach paves the way for application to the surveillance of land-based industry activities.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a new method for estimating ship micro-motion (m-m) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. Motion and m-m detection are typically addressed with SAR along-track interferometry using two radars separated by an azimuth baseline. Here, m-m estimation for ships spanning thousands of pixels is performed by exploiting information produced during the coregistration of multiple resynthesized, non-overlapping Doppler sub-apertures in the time domain. In particular, the SAR products are obtained by splitting the raw data with a temporally short baseline from a single wide-band staring spotlight (ST) SAR image. The main vibrational modes of different ships are then estimated. Performance is evaluated on one ST SAR image acquired by the COSMO-SkyMed satellite system. The proposed approach also opens the way to monitoring land-based industrial activities.
